ARK’s updated open-source Tesla model yields an expected value of ~$4,400 per share in 2031. The bull and bear cases—the 75th and 25th percentile Monte Carlo outcomes—are ~$5,000 and ~$3,300 per share, respectively, as shown below. The model draws on distributions across 32 independent inputs to simulate a range of outcomes for the company and its stock. Note: “EBITDA” is Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation, and Amortization. “CAGR” is Compound Annual Growth Rate. These forecasts do not reflect any fees or expenses related to owning Tesla shares.Overview And Key TakeawayARK estimates that Robotaxi will account for ~80% of Tesla’s enterprise value in 2031, down from ~90% in 2029 as presented in our previous model published in 2024.1 The primary reason is that we believe Optimus Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) is likely to inflect as robotaxis continue to proliferate, as shown below.Source: ARK Investment Management LLC, 2026. These forecasts do not reflect any fees or expenses related to owning Tesla shares.What’s Changed Since ARK’s Last Model Update?Robotaxi LaunchRobotaxi Pricing AssumptionsOptimus ContributionAI Infrastructure & Terafab SpendModel SimplificationsRobotaxi LaunchTesla launched its robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, in June 2025,2 matching the most probable launch year in our prior model. Since then, Tesla has scaled to seven cities across three states,3 and has completed more than 1 million unsupervised driverless miles in ~7 months, ~4x faster than Waymo’s first million, as shown below.4 Tesla expects the ramp to accelerate with Full Self-Driving (FSD) V15 late this year. Tesla has framed FSD V15 as the gating factor for scaling its robotaxi service.Source: ARK Investment Management LLC, 2026. For informational purposes only and should not be considered investment advice or a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any particular security. Past performance is not indicative of future results.Notably, Tesla added the Cybercab to its robotaxi fleet.5 Thanks to its vertical integration and vision-only approach to autonomous driving, our research suggests that, at equal utilization rates, Tesla’s operational costs per mile will be ~40% lower than those for Waymo’s next-gen robotaxi, as shown below. Tesla also could scale its robotaxi supply through consumer-owned vehicles, which would increase utilization and lower operating costs further. In our base case, Tesla deploys ~8 million robotaxis cumulatively by 2031.Source: ARK Investment Management LLC, 2026. Forecasts are inherently limited and cannot be relied upon as a basis for making an investment decision and are built on our modeling that reflect our biases and long-term positive view of the company. For informational purposes only and should not be considered investment advice or a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any particular security.Robotaxi Pricing AssumptionsAccording to our research, autonomous robotaxis could expand the ride-hail market well beyond today’s human-driven market. Highly utilized, cost-efficient robotaxis should be able to operate profitably at prices below those of ride-hail services today, making on-demand transportation accessible to a much broader swath of the population.This year, we refined our estimates of the robotaxi market at different price points using willingness-to-pay segmented by income. Our updated analysis captures a wider range of customer willingness-to-pay than our previous model. Although dynamic pricing could add to the upside, we have excluded it from our model to be conservative. That said, higher-income consumers travel disproportionately during congested periods, which could support higher peak-demand pricing. In other words, a robotaxi network could monetize riders with a higher willingness-to-pay during periods of constrained capacity and then lower prices during periods of less congestion to expand access and utilization across the broader market.Optimus ContributionElon has called Optimus Tesla’s largest long-term value driver,6 a view our research corroborates. Humanoid robots could scale to a ~$26 trillion total addressable market, roughly twice that of the robotaxis’ $10-15 trillion.7 In our 2024 model, we projected that internal deployments of ~30,000 humanoids would save Tesla ~$3.5 billion in costs in 2029. In our current model, external humanoid robot sales scale to ~1 million and generate ~$200 billion in RaaS revenues in 2031. Notably, ARK’s forecast is much more conservative than Elon’s guidance of 100 million to one billion Optimus units in 2031.8 Informed partly by the slower-than-expected rate of Tesla’s robotaxi progress, Optimus robots could reach human-level proficiency by ~2031, as shown below. Today, the industry’s primary bottleneck is real-world training data. Training data for Optimus is more difficult to collect than that of robotaxis because, unlike cars, humanoid robots have limited utility when manually operated and will not sell before meeting technical milestones. To address the data gap, Tesla has launched Optimus Academy to train 20,000 to 30,000 robots internally on various tasks. With vertically integrated vehicle factories that can offer real-world training and testing for Optimus, Tesla has an advantage relative to its competitors.9After reaching manufacturability and safety milestones, Tesla’s humanoid robot capability is likely to scale with compute, as shown below. Based on our research, Optimus will hit human level proficiency at ~4,000 MW (megawatts) or ~4 GW (gigawatts) of compute in 2031.Source: ARK Investment Management LLC, 2026. Past performance is not indicative of future results.AI Infrastructure & Terafab SpendSince the publication of our 2024 model, the AI race has intensified, with power and compute now the key differentiators. In our 2026 model, a new AI infrastructure line item drives the performance of Optimus. According to Elon, chip supply—for inference and training compute—will be the long-term constraint. Accordingly, Tesla and SpaceX have agreed to launch Terafab jointly.10 SpaceX is likely to foot a larger portion of the yet-to-be-announced capital commitment as it will develop the high-volume terrestrial and orbital manufacturing footprint, while Tesla focuses on building the initial research arm at an estimated cost of $3 billion.11 Our model assumes that Tesla will scale its spending on AI infrastructure from ~$7 billion cumulatively as of December 2025 to ~$225 billion by the end of 2031, as shown below.Source: ARK Investment Management LLC, 2026. Forecasts are inherently limited and cannot be relied upon as a basis for making an investment decision and are built on our modeling that reflect our biases and long-term positive view of the company. For informational purposes only and should not be considered investment advice or a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any particular security.Model SimplificationsWe have simplified the model since our last update by removing business lines like human-driven ride-hail and insurance, with a de minimis impact on Tesla’s price target. In addition, Tesla is likely to prioritize its Robotaxi operations in the US relative to China thanks to higher ride-hail pricing power and greater profit potential. Accordingly, we have removed its China Robotaxi operations from our model. Finally, accounting for the full dilution associated with Elon’s stock-based compensation, we also assume that it will vest within the valuation period, a win-win in our view!Business Opportunities Not Included In The ModelTesla SemiIn September 2026, volume production of the Semi began at Giga Nevada.12 Already, Tesla has an order for ~2,500 trucks, nearly double the entire Electric Class 8 fleet in the US.13 While autonomous trucking could represent a $320 billion addressable market by 2030, Tesla has signaled that it will prioritize high-volume robotaxi vehicles, a market that we estimate will be ~12X the size at scale.14FSD LicensingAt ~1.5 million active subscriptions as of June 30, 2026, and availability expanding across 8 European countries, FSD adoption continues to expand. That said, most of Tesla’s value is likely to accrue from its commercial robotaxi service rather than FSD licenses to Tesla customers and third parties.Tesla and SpaceX MergerWhile our model assesses Tesla as a standalone business, a SpaceX-Tesla merger could take place within the next five years. Tesla’s highly cash-generative robotaxi network could help fund SpaceX’s ambitious plans for orbital data centers, and at the same time SpaceX’s compute-intensive frontier AI models could serve as the planning layer for Optimus deployments. Working together on the Terafab project, both companies could alleviate chip constraints. Combined, we estimate that SpaceX and Tesla could generate $3.8 trillion in revenue and $2.7 trillion in EBIT15 by 2031, with SpaceX contributing roughly 62% and 69%, respectively, as shown below.Source: ARK Investment Management LLC, 2026. Note: Shares may not sum to 100% due to rounding. SpaceX launch is not directly material to 2031 revenue or EBIT results. Forecasts are inherently limited and cannot be relied upon as a basis for making an investment decision and are built on our modeling that reflect our biases and long-term positive view of the company. For informational purposes only and should not be considered investment advice or a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any particular security. Risks And Limits Of Our ModelThe primary risk to our forecast is a slower-than-expected ramp in robotaxi operations in response to regulatory delays or unexpected events—Elon Musk’s sudden departure, a natural disaster, or a pandemic. Now that robotaxis are becoming safer than human-driven cars, regulatory risks seem to be diminishing. ConclusionARK’s price target for Tesla in 2031 is ~$4,400 per share. We have published our model on GitHub, and we invite readers to explore and test our assumptions and/or create visualizations from the simulations.DisclosureThe forecasts and price estimates herein are subject to revision by ARK Invest (“ARK”) and provided solely as a guide to current expectations. These forecasts rely on models, which have several inherent limitations, including: 1) reliance on a variety of data obtained from sources that are believed to be reliable, but might be incorrect, inaccurate or incomplete and ARK does not guarantee the accuracy or completeness of any information obtained from any third party, 2) potential inclusion of inherent model creation biases, data discrepancies and/or calculation errors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected, and 3) NO reflection of the impact that material economic and market factors might have had and do not involve market risk. The forecasts rely on assumptions, forecasts, estimates, modeling, algorithms and other data input by ARK, some of which relies on third-parties, that could be or prove over time to be incorrect, inaccurate or incomplete.The forecasts are based on a variety of criteria and assumptions, which might vary substantially, and involve significant elements of subjective judgment and analysis that reflect our own expectations and biases, which might prove invalid or change without notice. It is possible that other foreseeable events that were not taken into account could occur. The forecasts contained herein represent the application of the simulation models as currently in effect on the date first written above, and there can be no assurance that the models will remain the same in the future or that an application of the current models in the future will produce similar results because the relevant market and economic conditions that prevailed during the period will not necessarily occur. The results will not be updated as the models change, or any information upon which they rely changes. There are numerous other factors related to the markets in general or to the public equity security specifically that cannot be fully accounted for in the preparation of forecasts, all of which can adversely affect actual results. For these reasons, forecasted results will differ, and could differ significantly from actual results.
